rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-midad is ink for a writing vessel, lamp oil, or, by metaphor, the earth's fertilizer; al-madad is what supplies more of it.
rows.anchor: المداد : اسم ما تمد به الدواة من الحبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is treated generically as ink for God's words of knowledge and wisdom; it and even another like it would run out first.
rows.anchor: لو كتبت كلمات علم الله وحكمته وكان البحر مدادا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madādan is a specification (tamyiz), like saying one has his equal as a man; al-madad is what adds to the supply.
rows.anchor: والمدد مثل المداد ، وهو ما يمد به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to explain the phrase as another sea like it serving as ink.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : بمثله مدادا

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads maddan as the plural of muddah, the quantity of writing material a scribe draws on.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج : مددا ، بكسر الميم جمع مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unassigned reading has the verb with yāʾ: yanfadu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ينفد ) بالياء

rows.speaker: حيي بن أخطب
rows.claim: Huyayy ibn Akhtab alleged contradiction between calling granted wisdom abundant good and saying people received little knowledge; the verse answers that wisdom is abundant yet only a drop beside God's words.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قال حيي بن أخطب : في كتابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hoping for the Lord's meeting means expecting a meeting of approval and acceptance; alternatively, it means fearing an evil meeting.
rows.anchor: فمن كان يؤمل حسن لقاء ربه ، وأن يلقاه لقاء رضا وقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on associating anyone in worship means avoiding ostentation and seeking only God's face without admixture.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنهي عن الإشراك بالعبادة : أن لا يرائي بعمله

rows.speaker: جندب ابن زهير
rows.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed about Jundub ibn Zuhayr, who said that he worked for God but was pleased when others saw his work; the Prophet answered that God does not accept a shared deed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في جندب ابن زهير ، قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : إني أعمل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises two rewards, for a hidden deed and a public one, when the person intends others to follow the example.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه قال : ( لك أجران : أجر السر ، وأجر العلانية )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls ostentation the lesser associating of partners, in response to a question about lesser shirk.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وما الشرك الأصغر ؟ قال : ( الرياء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises light from head to foot to one who recites the end of Surat al-Kahf, and light from earth to heaven to one who recites all of it.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الكهف من آخرها كانت له نورا من قرنه إلى قدمه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises a shining light and angels' prayers for one who recites this verse at bedtime, with the light reaching the Sacred House for a sleeper in Mecca.
rows.anchor: من قرأ عند مضجعه : { قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم }

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ with fatḥ and the yāʾ with kasr in Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād.
rows.anchor: قرأ بفتح الهاء وكسر الياء حمزة ، وبكسرهما عاصم

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads both the hāʾ and yāʾ with kasr.
rows.anchor: وبكسرهما عاصم ، وبضمهما الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads both the hāʾ and yāʾ with damm.
rows.anchor: وبكسرهما عاصم ، وبضمهما الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads dhikru rahmati rabbika, construing the recited passage as a mention of the Lord's mercy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ذكر رحمة ربك ) أي : هذا المتلو من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes dhikr an imperative: remember your Lord's mercy.
rows.anchor: من القرآن ذكر رحمة ربك وقرىء : ( ذكر ) على الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya follows God's practice of concealing supplication; concealment is preferable because public and private speech are equal before God, while privacy is farther from ostentation and more sincere.
rows.anchor: راعى سنة الله في إخفاء دعوته ، لأن الجهر والإخفاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains the hidden call as a prayer without ostentation.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن نداء لا رياء فيه ، أو أخفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Zakariya hid his request to avoid blame for asking for a child in old age.
rows.anchor: أو أخفاه لئلا يلام على طلب الولد في إبان الكبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he kept the prayer from the relatives whose conduct he feared.
rows.anchor: أو أسره من مواليه الذين خافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that his voice was weak from frailty and old age.
rows.anchor: أو خفت صوته لضعفه وهرمه ، كما جاء في صفة الشيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported estimates of Zakariya's age are sixty, sixty-five, seventy, seventy-five, and eighty-five.
rows.anchor: واختلف في سن زكريا عليه السلام ، فقيل : ستون ، وخمس وستون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb wahan is read with each of the three vowel patterns.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( وهن ) بالحركات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya singles out the bone because it is the body's pillar and foundation; if its strongest support weakens, the body's remaining strength falls with it.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر العظم لأنه عمود البدن وبه قوامه وهو أصل بنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular al-ʿaẓm expresses the whole category of bones; a plural would instead emphasize that all his bones, not just some, had weakened.
rows.anchor: ووحده لأن الواحد هو الدال على معنى الجنسية

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the sīn into the shīn in the recitation.
rows.anchor: إدغام السين في الشين عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gray hair is likened to flame for its whiteness, brightness, spread through the hair, and engulfing reach; the metaphor then attributes burning to the head, the hair's source.
rows.anchor: شبه الشيب بشواظ النار في بياضه وإنارته وانتشاره في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayban is set off as a specification and al-raʾs is left without a possessive because the hearer knows it is Zakariya's head; this makes the clause eloquent.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الشيب مميزا ولم يضف الرأس : اكتفاء بعلم المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya appeals to God's past responses to his needs; the author illustrates this with a needy person recalling a past kindness and receiving help.
rows.anchor: توسل إلى الله بما سلف لمعه من الاستجابة . وعن بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mawālī are Zakariya's relatives, brothers and cousins, whom he feared would alter the religion and fail as stewards; he sought a righteous descendant to revive its practice after his death.
rows.anchor: كان مواليه وهم عصبته إخوته وبنو عمه شرار بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads min warāʾi with a shortened final alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير : ( من وراي ) بالقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the standard reading, min warāʾi cannot attach directly to khift without spoiling the sense; it attaches to an omitted phrase, or describes the feared succession or those who take authority afterward.
rows.anchor: وهذا الظرف لا يتعلق بخفت لفساد المعنى ، ولكن بمحذوف

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman and Muhammad ibn Ali and Ali ibn al-Husayn read khiftu al-mawāli min warāʾi, which can mean the relatives behind Zakariya were few and weak, so he asked for a successor to support them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عثمان ومحمد بن علي وعلي بن الحسين رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: The same reading can construe warāʾi as before him: the relatives had died and none remained strong enough to help.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون بمعنى قدامي ، فيتعلق بخفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ladunka either intensifies that the requested heir is pleasing and comes from God, or asks for a miraculous gift without ordinary cause because neither spouse can conceive.
rows.anchor: { من لدنك } تأكيد لكونه وليا مرضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yarithni may be jussive as the response to the prayer, or nominative as an adjective.
rows.anchor: { يرثنى ويرث } الجزم جواب الدعاء ، والرفع صفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Jahdari read yarithuni wa arithu Āla Yaʿqub with the latter verb in the accusative as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والجحدري : يرثني وأرث آل يعقوب ، نصب

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jahdari's alternative aw yureth is a diminutive form of wāriṯ, meaning a small boy.
rows.anchor: وعن الجحدري : أويرث ، على تصغير وأرث

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali and others read wāriṯun min Āli Yaʿqūb, meaning that an heir from the family will inherit Zakariya; this is called tajrīd in rhetoric.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه وجماعة : وارث من آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance is prophetic law and knowledge, since prophets do not leave property as inheritance.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإرث إرث الشرع والعلم ، لأن الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says Zakariya's heir inherits the priestly office, while inheriting kingship from the family of Jacob.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يرثني الحبورة وكان حبرا ، ويرث من آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive because not every descendant of Jacob was a prophet or scholar; Zakariya descended from Jacob son of Isaac.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( من ) للتبعيض لا للتعدية ، لأن آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jacob named may be Jacob son of Isaac, Jacob son of Matan and Zakariya's brother, or Jacob and Mary's father Imran as brothers descended from Solomon.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو يعقوب بن ماتان أخو زكريا . وقيل : يعقوب هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one before Yahya bore the name Yahya; the author takes this as evidence that refined, distinguished names deserve preference.
rows.anchor: {سميا } لم يسم أحد بيحيى قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs sought noble and prominent names that avoided insulting nicknames, as in the cited poem praising elegant names and red robes.
rows.anchor: سنع الأسامي مسبلي أزر … حمر نمس الأرض بالهدب

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: When the genealogist al-Bakri asked Ruʾba for his lineage, Ruʾba answered that he was the son of al-ʿAjjaj; the reply said he had understated and identified himself.
rows.anchor: وقال رؤبة للنسابة البكري وقد سأله عن نسبه : أنا ابن العجاج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes samiyyan to mean an equal or counterpart, as in the question whether one knows any namesake of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مثلا وشبيها عن مجاهد ، كقوله : { هل تعلم له سميا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If these names are Arabic, Yahya's counterparts in naming include Yaʿmar and Yaʿish; people also named a man Yamut ibn al-Mizraʿ.
rows.anchor: ونحو : ( يحيى ) في أسمائهم ( يعمر ، ويعيش )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said Yahya had no equal because he never disobeyed or even intended sin, was born to an aged man and barren woman, and was chasur.
rows.anchor: قالوا : لم يكن له مثل في أنه لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya says his wife had been barren when he was young and middle-aged; now both causes of childlessness apply, making his question a request for explanation, not a change in belief.
rows.anchor: أي كانت على صفة العقر حين أنا شاب وكهل ، فما رزقت الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers so believers gain certainty and deniers are restrained; Zakariya's belief remained that God needs no causes.
rows.anchor: ليجاب بما أجيب به ، فيزداد المؤمنون إيقانا ويرتدع المبطلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtiyyan means dryness and hardness in joints and bones like withered wood, caused by advanced old age; alternatively, it denotes reaching the stages of old age called ʿatiyy.
rows.anchor: أي بلغت عتيا : وهو اليبس والجساوة في المفاصل والعظام

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read ʿitiyyan with kasr, as they do ṣilliyyan in 19:70.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي بكسر العين ، وكذلك { صليا }

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads both words with fatḥ.
rows.anchor: وابن مسعود بفتحهما فيهما

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy and Mujahid read ʿasiyyan instead of ʿitiyyan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ومجاهد ( عسيا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika may be nominative, meaning the matter is as stated, followed by qala rabbuk; or accusative with qala, pointing to the matter explained by huwa ʿalayya hayyin.
rows.anchor: { كذالك } الكاف رفع ، أي الأمر كذلك تصديق له ، ثم ابتدأ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads wa-huwa ʿalayya hayyin; this works only with the nominative analysis and means that what Zakariya said is indeed easy for God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( وهو علي هين ) ، ولا يخرج هذا إلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhālika points to God's preceding promise rather than Zakariya's statement; qala is elided in both readings, and its subject may be left implicit because God is speaking.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر : وهو أن يشار بذلك إلى ما تقدم من وعد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayʾan means either that the nonexistent is not a thing, or something insignificant, as in ordinary speech and the cited line of poetry.
rows.anchor: { شيئا } لأن المعدوم ليس بشيء . أو شيئا يعتد به

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, al-Kisaʾi, and Ibn Waththab read khalaqnāk instead of khalaqtuka.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش والكسائي وابن وثاب ( خلقناك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks for a sign by which he can know the promised event has occurred; the sign is being unable to speak despite sound limbs and no defect of speech.
rows.anchor: أي اجعل لي علامة أعلم بها وقوع ما بشرت به . قال : علامتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three nights here and three days in 3:41 indicate that the speech restriction lasted three days and their nights.
rows.anchor: دل ذكر الليالي هنا ، والأيام في آل عمران ، على أن المنع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya signaled to them; the expression is supported by the word ramzan in 3:41.
rows.anchor: أوحى : أشار عن مجاهد ، ويشهد له { إلا رمزا }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zakariya wrote sabbiḥū on the ground, meaning pray.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : كتب لهم على الأرض { سبحوا } صلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sabbiḥū is understood in its apparent sense, with an as that introduces the explanation.
rows.anchor: أو على الظاهر ، وأن : هي المفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is told to take the Torah seriously and preserve it with divine enabling and support.
rows.anchor: أي خذ التوراة بجد واستظهار بالتوفيق والتأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥukm means wisdom; a cited poetic phrase using aḥkamu supplies linguistic evidence.
rows.anchor: { الحكم } الحكمة . ومنه : وآحكم كحكم فتاة الحي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains wisdom here as understanding the Torah and religious jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: وهو الفهم للتوراة والفقه في الدين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says that when children invited Yahya to play, he answered that they were not created for play.
rows.anchor: وقيل : دعاء الصبيان إلى اللعب وهو صبي فقال : ما للعب خلقنا

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Maʿmar explains al-ḥukm as intellect.
rows.anchor: ما للعب خلقنا ، عن الضحاك . وعن معمر : العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is prophethood: God made Yahya's intellect firm in childhood and revealed to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل النبوة ، لأن الله أحكم عقله في صباه وأوحى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanānan means mercy toward his parents and others, expressed as tenderness and compassion.
rows.anchor: رحمة لأبويه وغيرهما ، وتعطفا وشفقة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh cites a poem in which Hanan is addressed as someone asked what brought him there and whether he knows the people.
rows.anchor: وقالت حنان ما أتى بك ههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative construes ḥanānan as God's compassion toward Yahya; ḥanna first means longing, then came to mean tender concern and pity.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حنانا من الله عليه . وحن : في معنى ارتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Ḥannān is metaphorical, just as calling Him Raḥīm is.
rows.anchor: وقيل لله ( حنان ) كما قيل : ( رحيم ) على سبيل الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh is interpreted either as purity or as almsgiving, describing Yahya's kindness and charity toward people.
rows.anchor: والزكاة : الطهارة ، وقيل الصدقة ، أي : يتعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Yahya peace in the three vulnerable states named in the verse: birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: سلم الله عليه في هذه الأحوال

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyaynah calls these the loneliest and most frightening circumstances.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عيينة : إنها أوحش المواطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the eastern place is an inclusive apposition to Maryam, since times include the events within them; the story focuses on this remarkable moment.
rows.anchor: { إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا } بدل من { ابن مريم } بدل الاشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intibādh means withdrawing into solitude; Maryam secluded herself for worship east of Jerusalem or apart from people in her house.
rows.anchor: والانتباذ : الاعتزال والانفراد ، تخلت للعبادة في مكان مما يلي شرقي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account places Maryam in an elevated chamber to wash after menstruation, screened by a wall; she stayed with her aunt while menstruating and returned to the mosque when pure.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قعدت في مشرفة للاغتسال من الحيض محتجبة بحائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel appeared during her ritual washing as a handsome, beardless young man with a complete, well-proportioned human form.
rows.anchor: فبينا هي في مغتسلها أتاها الملك في صورة آدمي شاب أمرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He appeared as a human so she would feel at ease speaking and would not recoil; an angelic appearance would have frightened her and prevented her hearing him.
rows.anchor: وإنما مثل لها في صورة الإنسان لتستأنس بكلامه ولا تنفر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her seeking refuge from such a beautiful figure demonstrates chastity and piety; the appearance tested her chastity.
rows.anchor: ودل على عفافها وورعها أنها تعوذت بالله من تلك الصورة الجميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Maryam lived in a separate sanctuary at her sister's husband Zakariya's home and left for solitude in the mountain; the roof opened and the angel came to her there.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت في منزل زوج أختها زكريا ولها محراب على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account says the angel stood before her as a servant of the sanctuary named Yusuf, a peer of hers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قام بين يديها في صورة ترب لها اسمه يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Christians are said to have adopted the east as their direction of prayer because Maryam withdrew to an eastern place.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن النصارى اتخذت المشرق قبله لانتباذ مريم مكانا شرقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, since religion is brought to life through him and revelation.
rows.anchor: الروح : جبريل ، لأن الدين يحيا به وبوحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God calls Gabriel His Spirit metaphorically out of love and honor, as one tells a beloved person, “you are my soul.”
rows.anchor: أو سماه الله روحه على المجاز محبة له وتقريبا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywah reads rūḥanā with fatḥ, because Gabriel is a cause of spiritual life and of receiving the promised spirit in 56:89; it can also mean one whom God draws near.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة : ( روحنا ) بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam means that if he is someone who fears and honors God, he will heed her appeal to seek refuge; she is taking refuge in God from him.
rows.anchor: أرادت إن كان يرجى منك أن تتقي الله وتخشاه وتحفل بالاستعاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger says he is sent by the One in whom she sought refuge; his role is to cause the gift of a boy by blowing into her garment.
rows.anchor: أي إنما أنا رسول من استعذت به { لاهب لك } لأكون سببا في هبة الغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some copies read that the Lord's messenger was commanded to give her the boy; alternatively, this wording recounts God's own speech.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف : إنما أنا رسول ربك أمرني أن أهب لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mass is a euphemism for lawful intercourse, as in 2:237 and 4:43; adultery is not referred to with such decorous euphemisms.
rows.anchor: جعل المس عبارة عن النكاح الحلال ، لأنه كناية عنه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad analyzes baghiyy as the feminine faʿūl form baghwī, with wāw assimilated into yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والبغي : الفاجرة التي تبغي الرجال ، وهي فعول عند المبرد ( بغوي )

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni instead analyzes baghiyy as faʿīl; if it were faʿūl, it would be baghū, like nahū.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جنى في كتاب التمام : هي فعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause “to make him a sign” has an omitted rationale, or coordinates with an omitted rationale such as demonstrating God's power; parallels occur at 45:22 and 12:21.
rows.anchor: { ولنجعله ءاية } تعليل معلله محذوف أي : ولنجعله آية للناس فعلنا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqḍiyyan means decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet, so it must occur; alternatively, the matter fittingly comes to pass as sign and mercy.
rows.anchor: { مقضيا } مقدرا مسطورا في اللوح لا بد لك من جريه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is a lesson and proof of God's power; the mercy comprises revealed laws and divine kindness that strengthen belief and lead to obedience and good deeds.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالآية : العبرة والبرهان على قدرة الله . وبالرحمة : الشرائع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Maryam felt reassured by the angel; he approached and blew into the opening of her garment, and the breath reached her womb, so she conceived.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فاطمأنت إلى قوله فدنا منها فنفخ في جيب درعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported pregnancy durations include six months; seven months according to Ata, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Dahhak; eight months, with Jesus the only infant said to survive an eight-month birth; and three hours.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت مدة الحمل ستة أشهر . وعن عطاء وأبي العالية والضحاك : سبعة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says conception, formation, and birth each took an hour, with birth at midday; Ibn Abbas also reports a single hour from conception to birth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حملته في ساعة ، وصور في ساعة ، ووضعته في ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reportedly Maryam conceived at age thirteen or ten and had menstruated twice before conceiving.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حملته وهي بنت ثلاث عشرة سنة . وقيل : بنت عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People say every newborn cries at birth except Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : ما من مولود إلا يستهل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fantabadhat bihi means she withdrew while carrying him; the preposition makes a circumstantial phrase, as in the cited poem and 23:20, where the plant grows with its oil.
rows.anchor: { فانتبذت به } أي اعتزلت وهو في بطنها ، كقوله : تدوس بنا الجماجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣiyyan means far away from her people beyond the mountain, or at the far end of the house.
rows.anchor: { قصيا } بعيدا من أهلها وراء الجبل . وقيل : أقصى الدار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: One story says Maryam fled with her cousin Yusuf after people accused her of fornication; when he considered killing her, Gabriel told him the child was from the Holy Spirit, so he spared her.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت سميت لابن عم لها اسمه يوسف ، فلما قيل : حملت من الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajāʾa derives from jāʾa but, after causative transfer, means forcing someone to come; the author compares it with forms meaning to make someone reach or give something.
rows.anchor: {فأجاءها } أجاء : منقول من جاء ، إلا أن استعماله قد تغير

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: In one narration, Ibn Kathir reads al-mikhāḍ with kasr; it denotes the fetus's movement in the womb.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية ( المخاض ) بالكسر . يقال : مخضت الحامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She sought the trunk to screen and brace herself during delivery; the author pictures a dry, bare palm trunk in the winter desert.
rows.anchor: طلبت الجذع لتستتر به وتعتمد عليه عند الولادة ، وكان جذع نخلة يابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nakhlah may be a proper-name-like definite expression for a locally known tree, or a generic definite referring to the particular palm God directed her to for nourishing postpartum dates.
rows.anchor: والتعريف لا يخلو : إما أن يكون من تعريف الأسماء الغالبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm was chosen because its dates suit a woman after childbirth, it is especially vulnerable to cold, and its fruit grows from its spadix, gathering signs in one tree.
rows.anchor: كأن الله تعالى إنما أرشدها إلى النخلة ليطعمها منها الرطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mātu is read with either ḍamm or kasr, both attested forms of the verb to die.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( مت ) بالضم والكسر ، يقال : مات يموت ومات يمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasyan is a disposable thing that should be cast away and forgotten, like a menstrual rag or similar trivial object; the author compares the noun pattern to dhabh in 37:107.
rows.anchor: النسي : ما من حقه أن يطرح وينسى ، كخرقة الطامث ونحوها

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus says travelers call small belongings left behind when moving, such as a stick or cup, ansāʾ; Maryam wished she were such a negligible forgotten thing.
rows.anchor: وعن يونس : العرب إذا ارتحلوا عن الدار قالوا : انظروا أنساءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her wish reflects intense shame and ordinary human distress, not rejection of God's decree; alternatively, she feared public slander despite knowing her innocence and divine honor, or feared people would sin through their accusations.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما لحقها من فرط الحياء والتشور من الناس على حكم العادة البشرية

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and Hafs read nasyan with fatḥ; al-Farrāʾ calls the two vowel forms dialect variants like watr and witr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة وحفص ( نسيا ) بالفتح

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi reads nasʾ with hamza, meaning milk diluted with water because it is scarce and thin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن كعب القرظي ( نسأ ) بالهمز

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads munsiyan with kasr on the second word's initial vowel by vowel-following assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( منسيا ) بالكسر على الإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min taḥtihā is explained as Gabriel, who acted like a midwife, or as Jesus; the latter is the reading of Asim and Abu Amr.
rows.anchor: {من تحتها } هو جبريل عليه السلام . قيل : كان يقبل كالقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min taḥtihā means below her position, as in the phrase about rivers flowing below; another account places the caller beneath a hill.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { تحتها } أسفل من مكانها ، كقوله : { تجرى من تحتها الانهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings reported from Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs keep min taḥtihā; the speaker in nādāhā may be the angel or Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص ( من تحتها )

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the pronoun in taḥtihā refers to the palm tree.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : الضمير في تحتها للنخلة

rows.speaker: زر
rows.claim: Zirr and ʿAlqama read fa-khāṭabahā, “he addressed her from beneath.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ زر وعلقمة : فخاطبها من تحتها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about al-sariyy, the Prophet said it is a stream; Labid's poem uses the word for a stream.
rows.anchor: ( 658 ) سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السري فقال : ( هو الجدول )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sariyy derives from sarw and refers to Jesus; al-Hasan says he was a noble servant.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من السرو . والمراد : عيسى وعن الحسن : كان والله عبدا سريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stream and dates console Maryam as miraculous signs of her purity and freedom from suspicion, showing her accusers that her virgin birth is part of extraordinary divine action.
rows.anchor: لم تقع التسلية بهما من حيث أنهما طعام وشراب ، ولكن من حيث أنهما معجزتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb tasāqaṭ has nine reported readings, varying assimilation, deletion, verb person, and whether the subject is the palm or trunk.
rows.anchor: { تساقط } فيه تسع قرآت : ( تساقط ) بإدغام التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruṭban is either a specification or a direct object, depending on the reading.
rows.anchor: ورطبا تمييز أو مفعول على حسب القراءة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad allows ruṭban to be governed by hazzi, though the author rejects this analysis.
rows.anchor: وعن المبرد : جواز انتصابه بهزي وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-jidhʿi either reinforces the construction, as in 2:195, or means to shake using the trunk, supported by the cited line about a blade wounding camels' hocks.
rows.anchor: والباء في { بجذع النخلة } صلة للتأكيد ، كقوله تعالى : { ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dates were customary food for a woman after childbirth and for tahnik; the dates were said to be ʿajwah, and sayings praise dates for postpartum women and honey for the ill.
rows.anchor: قالوا : التمر للنفساء عادة من ذلك الوقت ، وكذلك التحنيك

rows.speaker: طلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: Talha ibn Sulayman reads janiyyan with kasr by vowel-following assimilation.
rows.anchor: عن طلحة بن سليمان { جنيا } بكسر الجيم للإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stream and ripe dates provide nourishment and also console her because they are miracles; “eat, drink, and be comforted” means be at peace and abandon grief.
rows.anchor: الشرب ، والثانية سلوة الصدر ؛ لكونهما معجزتين . وهو في معنى قوله : { فكلى واشربى وقرى عينا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarri ʿaynan means be content and at ease; qirri is the Najdi dialect form.
rows.anchor: أي وطيبي نفسا ولا تغتمي وارفضي عنك ما أحزنك وأهمك

rows.speaker: ابن الرومي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Rumi reads tarayinna with hamza, a feature of speakers who say labaʾtu bi-l-ḥajj and ḥalaʾtu al-sawīq.
rows.anchor: { فإما ترين } بالهمز : ابن الرومي . عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawman means silence; Abd Allah's codex reads ṣamtan, as does a report from Anas. Another explanation is fasting, in which people did not speak.
rows.anchor: { صوما } صمتا . وفي مصحف عبد الله : صمتا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prohibited fasting in silence, which the author says was abrogated for his community.
rows.anchor: ( 659 ) ( نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صوم الصمت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam was instructed to vow silence to avoid speaking with people who suspected her: Jesus would vindicate her, and she would avoid arguing with fools; keeping silent before a fool is obligatory.
rows.anchor: أمرها الله بأن تنذر الصوم لئلا تشرع مع البشر المتهمين لها في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that Maryam told the people by gesture that she had vowed silence; alternatively, she was allowed to speak the vow aloud.
rows.anchor: قيل : أخبرتهم بأنها نذرت الصوم بالإشارة . وقيل : سوغ لها ذلك بالنطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insiyyan means a human being, in contrast to speaking to angels.
rows.anchor: { إنسيا } أي أكلم الملائكة دون الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fariyy means extraordinary or wondrous, from the cutting and preparation of leather.
rows.anchor: الفري : البديع ، وهو من فري الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation identifies the Harun addressed as Mary's brother from their father, one of the exemplary Israelites; another makes him Moses's brother.
rows.anchor: { فأرسل إلى هارون } كان أخاها من أبيها من أمثل بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the people meant Aaron the prophet, though Maryam was a descendant many generations later, by a thousand years or more.
rows.anchor: ( 660 ) ( إنما عنوا هرون النبي ) وكانت من أعقابه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Maryam was one of Aaron's descendants.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي : كانت من أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sister of Aaron” may mean a member of his people, as “brother of Hamdan” does, rather than a sibling by descent.
rows.anchor: وإنما قيل : يا أخت هرون ، كما يقال : يا أخا همدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, people compared or insulted Maryam by a righteous or wicked man named Aaron in her time; one righteous Aaron's funeral was followed by forty thousand namesakes honoring his name.
rows.anchor: وقيل : رجل صالح أو طالح في زمانها ، شبهوها به

rows.speaker: عمر بن لجأ التيمي
rows.claim: Umar ibn Laja al-Taymi reads mā kāna abāki imruʾu sawʾ, changing the case form in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن لجأ التيمي ( ما كان أباك امرؤ سوء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Yusuf al-Najjar took Maryam and Jesus to a cave for forty days until she recovered from childbirth; Jesus spoke to her on the way, and her pious household grieved when she returned.
rows.anchor: وقيل احتمل يوسف النجار مريم وابنها إلى غار ، فلبثوا فيه أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says her people nearly stoned her until the infant Jesus spoke, after which they left her alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هموا برجمها حتى تكلم عيسى عليه السلام . فتركوها
